title: 5.8.2 Sub-build: Two balls, two masses
description: The same push on two balls, one heavy and one light. Build it small, then feel the difference before you tune your table.

steps.title: Run it first
steps.instructions: Both balls sit still. Nothing pushes them and they have the same mass, so nothing tells them apart.

steps.title: Give them different masses
steps.instructions: Set `heavy.mass = 4;` and `light.mass = 0.5;` in `setup()`. Mass is how hard a thing is to push: the same force moves the light one much further.
hints: Set mass after the sprite exists, in `setup()`, not before.
A `static` sprite has no mass and ignores the setting.

steps.title: Push both the same
steps.instructions: In `draw()`, on `kb.presses('p')`, apply the same force to both: `heavy.applyForce(6, 0); light.applyForce(6, 0);`. Run it and press P: the light ball should shoot away and the heavy one barely move.
hints: If they move the same, the masses were set to the same value, or one ball is still `static`.
Try `gravityScale` on one ball too: 0.5 makes it float, 2 makes it sink faster.

requirements.title: Two different masses
requirements.description: Both balls get a mass, and the numbers differ. Help: 5.8.1 (Reading: Four knobs: mass, gravityScale, rotationLock, debug)

requirements.title: The same push reaches both
requirements.description: applyForce (or a velocity set) is called on both balls, so the comparison is fair. Help: 5.8.1 (Reading: Four knobs: mass, gravityScale, rotationLock, debug)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a short moSHion sketch for "Sub-build: Two balls, two masses". The task: give two balls different masses in setup() and apply the same force to both on a key press, so the difference in mass is what makes them move differently. This is a sub-build: a small isolated program whose only job is this one mechanic, so judge the mechanic itself and not style. Accept any variable names, helper functions, arrow functions, ternaries and semicolons. A line that only exists in a comment or a string does not count. moSHion facts: colliding(b) is 0 while apart and counts frames while touching, so an if on it alone is true every frame of a touch; a stored "last frame" value makes it true once. .life = n counts down one per frame and deletes the sprite at 0. A sprite with collider 'none' is passed through and has its gravity off. loadSound(path) in setup() and sound.play() where the event happens; a browser will not play sound before the student's first click or key. Write short, plain notes for a 14-year-old, name the student's own line when something is missing, and never write corrected code.

rubric.title: Different masses
rubric.description: Two sprites get .mass with different values, set after they exist.

rubric.title: One fair push
rubric.description: The same applyForce is called on both (or the same force number), so mass is the only variable.

rubric.title: It can be felt
rubric.description: The masses differ enough to see (roughly 0.5 against 4), and neither sprite is static.
